en.title: H
en.summary: The letter H is the eighth letter of the Romanian alphabet.

sections.title: The letter haș
paragraphs: The letter name is spoken as the sound /h/, that is a standard h sound. Its main sound appears in the word (hartă) /harˈtə/, which means map. This letter produces three sounds in Romanian speech.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: For the first sound, breathe out gently through an open mouth. Keep your tongue relaxed and let air whisper past your throat. For the next sound, push the middle of your tongue close to the hard roof. Force the air through that narrow gap. For the last sound, raise the back of your tongue toward the soft palate. Breathe out with light friction. Place a hand on your throat to feel that your vocal cords stay completely still.

sections.title: Spelling rules
paragraphs: Before back vowels and at the start of most native words, say the sound /h/, that is a standard h sound, as in (horă) /ˈho.rə/. Before front vowels, pronounce the sound /ç/, that is a soft h sound, heard in (harnic) /ˈhar.nik/ and (hienă) /ˈhje.nə/. At the end of a word or before consonants, speak the sound /x/, like in (valah) /vaˈlah/ or (duh) /duh/.

sections.title: Comparing with English
paragraphs: English speakers often drop this letter because of words like hour or honest. In Romanian, you must always pronounce it clearly. The sound at the end of words is stronger than the sound in house. Do not make it silent like the h in vehicle. Move your tongue further back and push steady air through your mouth.
